catalog_quote: Most notably, tone is not directly transcribed. This is because the tonal system of at least one variety of Bumthang (Ura) is very complex, involving more than eight contrasts which are susceptible to change due to intonation and the presence of tonally-signalled morphology, and so not amenable to annotation in a survey context.8 As far as it makes sense to speak of stress in a language with contrastive tone, stress is initial, and trochaic. [fn. 8] For instance, five levels are attested in the Ura Bumthang words nu55 ‘soot’, lɔŋ44 ‘wind’, mi33 ‘person’, ŋɔj22 ‘silver’, jam11 ‘path’. The same dialect also has contour tones, including those attested in na52 ‘head of queue’, ɲam343 ‘fat’, and wam334 ‘bear’. While segmentally distinct, all of the consonants are sonorants, and there is nothing in the different segments involved that would be responsible for the different pitch contours.
world_status: statement found in an open source

Footnote 8 (five level tones n…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bumthang is a language with contrastive (complex, multi-level) lexical and morphological tone; to the extent stress can be identified at all, it falls on the initial syllable, with trochaic rhythm.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing explicit; 'trochaic' implies alternating strong-weak footing from the left edge but no secondary-stress statement is made.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The author hedges the very applicability of 'stress' in a contrastive-tone language.
new_statements.domain_note: A one-sentence remark in the transcription conventions of a dialect wordlist survey (seven East Bodish varieties: Chamkhar, Dhur, Chumey, Tang, Ura, Trongsa Bumthang plus Henkha); word-level, based on elicited citation forms; no phonetic evidence or examples given for stress. van Driem's 2015 grammar (the fullest description) treats only high/low register tone and is silent on stress; Peck 2017 defines the Bumthang prosodic word by a single tonal contour.
new_statements.identity_note: Donohue 2020's remark is made for the Bumthang dialect survey as a whole (Chamkhar, Dhur, Chumey, Tang, Ura and Trongsa varieties of Bumthang, ISO kjz = bumt1240, plus a Henkha/Nyenkha list, ISO neh = nyen1254); the tone detail cited is specifically Ura Bumthang. van Driem 2015 describes standard Bumthang of the four valleys (Chogor, Chunmat, Tang, Ura speakers).

tone_statements.quote: 小論での音韻表記について：先行研究で指摘されているように、ブムタン語には、鼻音、流音、半母音、母音始まりの音節では、高低の 2 声調の区別が存在する。以下の記述では、高声調の音節に、Hɲit、Hli のようにマークをつけて表記する。
tone_statements.translation: On the phonological transcription used in this paper: as pointed out in previous studies, Bumthang has a distinction of two tones, high and low, in syllables beginning with a nasal, liquid, semivowel or vowel. In the description below, high-tone syllables are marked as in Hɲit, Hli.

tone_statements.summary: Two tones, high vs low (register-type), contrastive only on syllables with nasal, liquid, glide or vowel onsets (implying pitch is predictable after obstruents); high tone written with a prefixed H on the syllable; no contours, TBU, downstep or stress discussed.
